entries.clue: One who grinds corn for flour; a red-bearded brawler who butts doors off the hinge
Great church of a bishop; the one at their journey's end held the martyr's bones
Thick and slow-flowing, like cold honey tipped from a jar
Geoffrey who began the work about 1387 and died in 1400 with it unfinished
Pig's bones in glass and a pillowcase called Our Lady's veil, sold as holy
London's underground railway, or the hollow passage a molten stream leaves behind
Nylon strap held tight in the waiting room so the dog cannot bolt
Small cat carried in hissing, protected against cat flu from about nine weeks
Compulsory for dogs since 2016 and for cats in England since 2024: a rice-grain implant
Sum charged for the consultation, payable at the desk on the way out
Coarse specks that settle on cars for miles around a blast, or plain dogged determination
Unhopped malt brew of the day; one rider is too full of it to wait his turn
Sleeping for now though not dead, of a bulb in winter or a quiet mountain
